source.title: Searched 2026-10-29, nothing covers 1650-1730: (1) gunsmith tools 17th c. with Moxon, Mechanick Exercises (joiner, smith, turner and carpenter tools, no gunmaking); (2) Colonial Williamsburg gunsmith shop (18th-c. reconstruction; only date before 1730 is John Brush's shop of 1717, American Rifleman article, no tool list for the period); (3) Royal Armouries and English gunmakers (Bailey and Nie, Blackmore: trade history, no tools; PDF unreadable); (4) 17th-c. gunmaker probate inventories (none found); (5) Colonial Williamsburg 'Tools of the Trades' (403); (6) Randle Holme, The Academy of Armory (1688), book III: read the Metal Workers chapter (book III ch. 7, rholme.taths.org.uk transcription): it lists hammer, pincers, anvil, keys and household locks and names no gunsmith or firearm; a search of the transcription found no gunsmith page, and the 1688 printing stops at book III ch. 13, the rest being printed in 1905. (7) task 2519, pages opened by direct fetch: the EEBO-TCP Holme 1688 text (quod.lib.umich.edu, A44150 and A44230 table of contents) returned 403 and the Oxford EEBO-TCP record (llds.phon.ox.ac.uk, A44230) returned a bot-protection page, so no 'Hand-Gun' maker entry could be opened or searched; a web search found only catalogue records for it. The 1905 Roxburghe Club edition (ed. Jeayes, book III from ch. 14) has a Google Books record with no viewable pages, a HathiTrust full-text search returned 403 and the archive.org item search found nothing, so it stayed unreadable and the Roxburghe volume's gunsmith passage, if any, is unchecked. Diderot Encyclopedie 'Arquebusier' (plates 1751-72, after the period, a note only): the ARTFL and Wikimedia Commons category pages tried returned 404 or an unrelated page, so the plate explanation was not read; no tool list is taken from it
source.gives: no source found for gunsmith's tools in 1650-1730; later or reconstructed shops show a forge, anvil, vise, hand files, a flywheel boring bench and a rifling machine
